record.paper_title: Algorithmic Semi-algebraic Geometry and Topology -- Recent Progress and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Quantifier elimination for projected quadratic systems
record.original_question: Let S be a closed and bounded semi-algebraic subset of R^{k+m} defined by a fixed number ell of quadratic inequalities P_1 >= 0, ..., P_ell >= 0, where each P_i has degree at most 2, and let pi: R^{k+m} -> R^m be the projection onto the last m coordinates. Because pi(S) is semi-algebraic, quantifier elimination asks for a quantifier-free semi-algebraic description of pi(S). For fixed ell, can quantifier elimination for this class be performed efficiently, in particular in time polynomial in k and m?

evidence.quote: the image of a semi-algebraic set under a linear projection is semi-algebraic
it is not known whether quantifier elimination can be performed efficiently when the number of quadratic inequalities is kept constant.
let S ⊂ R k+m be a closed and bounded semi-algebraic set defined by P1 ≥ 0, . . . , P` ≥ 0, with Pi ∈ R[X1 , . . . , Xk , Y1 , . . . , Ym ], deg(Pi ) ≤ 2
there is no known algorithm for computing a semi-algebraic description of π(S) in time polynomial in k and m.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a positive integer $\ell$. Let $S \subset \mathbb{R}^{k+m}$ be a closed and bounded semi-algebraic set defined by
$$P_1 \ge 0,\; P_2 \ge 0,\; \dots,\; P_\ell \ge 0,$$
where each $P_i \in \mathbb{R}[X_1,\dots,X_k,Y_1,\dots,Y_m]$ has total degree at most $2$. Let $\pi : \mathbb{R}^{k+m} \to \mathbb{R}^m$ denote the projection onto the last $m$ coordinates $(Y_1,\dots,Y_m)$. By the Tarski–Seidenberg theorem, the image $\pi(S)$ is again a semi-algebraic subset of $\mathbb{R}^m$, so there exists a quantifier-free Boolean combination of polynomial inequalities in $Y_1,\dots,Y_m$ describing $\pi(S)$.

Question: For every fixed $\ell$, does there exist an algorithm which, given the polynomials $P_1,\dots,P_\ell$, computes a quantifier-free semi-algebraic description of $\pi(S)$ in time polynomial in $k$ and $m$?
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known: Basu and others have given polynomial-time algorithms (for fixed ℓ) for computing the top Betti numbers and bounding the Betti numbers of projections of semi-algebraic sets defined by a constant number of quadratic inequalities, and Barvinok gave polynomial-time feasibility algorithms for systems of quadratic equations with a fixed number of equations. However, no algorithm is known that produces a quantifier-free description of π(S) in time polynomial in k and m, even for fixed ℓ; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On Projections of Semi-Algebraic Sets Defined by Few Quadratic Inequalities
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm for computing first q Betti numbers of π(S) with complexity (k+m)^{2^{O(qℓ)}}, polynomial in k+m for fixed q and ℓ.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-time algorithms exist for topological invariants of π(S) for fixed ℓ, but not for full quantifier-free descriptions.

status_evidence.title: Feasibility testing for systems of real quadratic equations
status_evidence.snippet: Barvinok's algorithm decides feasibility of a fixed number of quadratic equations in time polynomial in the number of variables.
status_evidence.claim: For a fixed number of quadratic constraints, feasibility is in polynomial time, but quantifier elimination for projections is not addressed.
